# VFX UI Anime

> Fifteen expressive native Web Components, including eleven source-backed animated controls and four additional VFX UI Anime controls.

## Project map
- `index.html`: interactive component gallery with live controls and per-component usage prompts.
- `core.js`: additional VFX UI Anime effects engine used by Like, Accordion, Segmented, and Notification.
- `styles.css`: VFX UI Anime design tokens and product presentation.
- `components/<name>/index.js`: individual component implementation.
- `components/<name>/demo.html`: standalone live preview.
- `components/<name>/README.md`: component-specific API, behaviour, and limitations.
- `docs/COMPONENTS.md`: component inventory and engine architecture.
- `docs/COMPONENT_API_REFERENCE.md`: attributes, properties, events, and methods.
- `tests/browser.html`: browser test fixture.
- `tools/validate.mjs`: repository validation.

## Standalone animated controls
The following eleven controls include their own spring/effect engine and artwork. They do not depend on `core.js`.
- `components/button/`: `<vfx-button>`
- `components/toggle/`: `<vfx-toggle>`
- `components/slider/`: `<vfx-slider>`
- `components/checkbox/`: `<vfx-checkbox>`
- `components/radio/`: `<vfx-radio>`
- `components/input/`: `<vfx-input>`
- `components/tabs/`: `<vfx-tabs>`
- `components/progress/`: `<vfx-progress>`
- `components/rating/`: `<vfx-rating>`
- `components/toast/`: `<vfx-toast>`
- `components/tooltip/`: `<vfx-tooltip>`

Their embedded runtime is exposed as `window.VFXAnimeFX`. The Toggle contains its 43-frame painted animation in the component file.

## Additional VFX UI Anime controls
These four controls use `core.js`, which exposes `window.VFXAnime`.
- `components/like/`: `<vfx-like>`
- `components/accordion/`: `<vfx-accordion>`
- `components/segmented/`: `<vfx-segmented>`
- `components/notification/`: `<vfx-notification>`

## Integration rules
1. For Button through Tooltip, load each required component script directly.
2. For Like, Accordion, Segmented, or Notification, load `core.js` first.
3. Follow each component's README and demo for its exact API.
4. Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`.
5. Verify browser behaviour before making compatibility claims.
